messages:
nina: Quick report: customer reported Python SDK failing verification on Windows with CPython 3.8/3.9. Error: SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED when hitting their private gateway. Works on linux/mac.

raj: Does the user run from venv? Which certifi version? Windows can be weird if the wheel wasn't used.

nina: venv, pip-installed. certifi 2023.11.x. Tried python-certifi-win32, no luck.

michael: Hypothesis: their internal CA chain is missing an intermediate that some Windows OpenSSL builds won't fetch. Two mitigation paths: (A) allow pointing SDK at a full PEM bundle via env var REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE; (B) accept an ssl.SSLContext or path via new `verify` client option so ops can pass custom trust store.

raj: Also add a small Windows job in CI matrix (windows-latest, py3.8 and py3.11) running a TLS smoke test against a recorded endpoint. That'll catch regressions and wheel vs sdist issues.

nina: Can we also add a short troubleshooting blurb in DevEx docs listing: certifi, python-certifi-win32, REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE, and how to supply SSLContext? Customers hit this often.

michael: Agreed. I'll open a PR to add `verify` param (bool | str | ssl.SSLContext) and read REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE from env if set. Keep default behaviour unchanged.

ci-bot: Created issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-python-sdk/issues/551 "Windows py3.8/3.9: cert verification failures; add REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE + verify option" assigned to @michael

nina: Thanks. Workaround validated when I set REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE to our full-bundle.pem. Staging green. Will paste commands in the issue.

raj: One more note: we should document support policy for 3.8-3.12 and mention that Windows wheels reduce these platform-specific failures.

michael: Will include CI + docs + small example in examples/windows that shows both env var and passing SSLContext to the async client. Also adding a follow-up issue for typing stubs for the async client on Windows.

nina: Perfect. Closing the loop after the PR merges.
